Fig.
 5.
 Areas
 in
 which
 young
 adults
 (YA)
 exhibit
 more
 activation
 than
 older
 adults
(OA)
 during
 transfer
 of
 learning
 (run
 13).
 YA
 demonstrated
 greater
 activation
 in
 the
left
 putamen,
 right
 caudate
 nucleus,
 and
 left
 cingulate
 gyrus
 compared
 to
 OA.
 −34
 52
 
3.76
 score
Neither
 age
 group
 had
 any
 regions
 exhibiting
 greater
 activation
 at
transfer
 (run
 13)
 than
 learning
 (run
 3)
 which
 overlapped
 with
 their
respective
 SWM
 networks.
4.
 Discussion
The
 goal
 of
 the
 current
 study
 was
 to
 determine
 whether
 age
affects
 the
 extent
 to
 which
 individuals
 rely
 upon
 spatial
 working
memory
 for
 motor
 learning
 and
 transfer.
 Similar
 to
 our
 previous
results,
 we
 found
 that
 older
 adults
 exhibited
 equal
 or
 even
 better
transfer
 than
 young
 adults
 for
 some
 performance
 variables
 [10].
This
 is
 particularly
 striking
 given
 that
 older
 adults
 exhibited
 less
learning
 than
 the
 young
 adults
 and
 therefore
 had
 a
 theoretically
 less
well-formed
 motor
 representation
 to
 work
 with
 at
 motor
 transfer.
We
 also
 found
 that
 the
 underlying
 cognitive
 and
 neural
 correlates
of
 motor
 transfer
 differed
 for
 the
 two
 age
 groups.
